mathgap.title: Initial counts from 'has' statements
mathgap.principle: Treat statements of the form 'X has N items' as giving X's initial count before any transfers or other operations; they are not the final count after transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement directly states a person's count without mentioning any transfers or comparisons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Alice has 12 apples' as the final count after later transfers, leading to inconsistency.

mathgap.title: Apply transfers correctly
mathgap.principle: For each 'X gives K items to Y' statement, subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count, applying all transfers after establishing initial counts.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the transfer 'Bob gives 3 oranges to Carol' and leaving Bob's count unchanged.

mathgap.title: Direct comparison 'has K more than'
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has K more items than Y' as the equation X = Y + K, establishing a directed difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement directly compares two counts with a fixed offset.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 5 more than Y' as X = Y - 5, reversing the sign.

mathgap.title: Absolute difference for 'difference between'
mathgap.principle: Treat 'the difference between the number of items that A and B have' as the absolute value |A − B|, regardless of which is larger.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement refers to the difference between two persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between A and B' as A - B, which can be negative.

mathgap.title: Magnitude interpretation for 'has more than' in equality statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of items that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between A and B', interpret the left side as the positive magnitude X − Y (assuming X > Y) and set it equal to the absolute difference |A − B|.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a 'has more than' clause appears inside an equality that also mentions a 'difference between' clause.
mathgap.example: Assuming X > Y even when other constraints imply X < Y, leading to contradictory equations.

mathgap.title: Propagate known absolute differences
mathgap.principle: When a statement fixes an absolute difference (e.g., 'X has 9 more than Y'), propagate that as a constraint that |X − Y| = 9, allowing both possible orders unless direction is explicitly given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement provides a fixed difference without specifying direction.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has 9 more than Y' as X = Y + 9 only, ignoring the possibility that Y could be larger.

mathgap.title: Symbolic substitution over guessing
mathgap.principle: Set up a system of equations for all variables and solve them algebraically; avoid guessing specific values unless the system is underdetermined.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When multiple constraints interrelate many variables.
mathgap.example: Randomly picking a value for a variable without checking all constraints.

mathgap.title: Final consistency check
mathgap.principle: After obtaining a solution, verify that every original statement (including direction of inequalities) holds; if any statement fails, revise the solution.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system of equations.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution that violates 'Cliff has more than Carnell' without noticing the inconsistency.

mathgap.title: Use integer bounds to prune solutions
mathgap.principle: All counts are small non‑negative integers (typically 0‑30) and the answer lies between 10‑30; discard any solutions outside this range early to reduce the search space.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving for variables, apply domain constraints as soon as possible.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person's count is 45, which is outside the allowed range.

mathgap.title: Treat 'has more than' in equality statements as absolute difference
mathgap.principle: When a statement links a 'has more than' clause to a 'difference between' clause (e.g., 'The number of X that Y has more than Z equals the difference between A and B'), interpret the left side as the absolute magnitude |Y − Z| and set it equal to |A − B|, without assuming Y > Z even if the wording suggests it. This avoids contradictions when other constraints imply the opposite ordering.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'has more than' clause appears inside an equality that also mentions a 'difference between' clause, and there is a potential conflict with other statements about the ordering of the two persons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Cliff has more than Carnell' as Cliff − Carnell = |Rozella − Carrie|, which fails because Carnell > Cliff; the correct approach is |Cliff − Carnell| = |Rozella − Carrie|.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has' statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that the count given in a 'has' statement already includes later transfers, ignoring that transfers modify the count later.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'has' statements as initial counts before any transfers; apply transfers separately.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'has K more than' as X = Y - K
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reverses the direction of the offset, subtracting instead of adding.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'X has K more than Y' as X = Y + K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets the phrase as A - B, which can be negative, instead of the absolute difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'difference between A and B' as |A - B|.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the effect of transfer statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model overlooks 'gives' statements, leaving counts unchanged.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer by subtracting from the giver and adding to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Assuming direction in 'has more than' equality statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats the left side of a 'has more than' clause inside an equality as a signed difference (X - Y) and assumes X > Y, even when other constraints imply X < Y, leading to contradictions.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret the left side as an absolute magnitude |X - Y| and set it equal to the absolute difference on the right side, without enforcing X > Y.
